children.definition: to do something illegal or wrong
a person who sees a crime or an accident happen
children.example: Police are asking witnesses to come forward.

children.definition: (of the police) to take someone away because they may have broken the law
children.example: Two men were arrested near the bank.

children.definition: a person who the police think may have committed a crime
children.example: The main suspect has left the country.

children.definition: facts or objects that show that something is true
children.example: There was not enough evidence to prove that he was guilty.

children.definition: having done something illegal, according to a court
children.example: The court found her guilty of theft.

children.definition: not having done the crime that someone is accused of
children.example: He insisted that he was innocent.

children.definition: the punishment that a judge gives someone
children.example: She received a two-year prison sentence.

children.definition: money that you must pay as a punishment
children.example: I got a fine for parking in the wrong place.
Report any theft to the police immediately.

children.definition: the crime of tricking people in order to get money
children.example: Online fraud often starts with a fake message from a 'bank'.

children.definition: the place where a judge decides whether someone is guilty
children.example: The case will go to court next month.
